page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-56 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server provides 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 112 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not feature local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage options.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core processing capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU tests. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets, which is reflected in its strong Passmark CPU encryption score. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth ranks in the top 25%, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the middle 50% tier. For specialized workloads, the server achieves strong results in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, alongside high throughput in Redis SET operations and small-to-medium scale LLM text generation.

From a resource allocation perspective, the c2d-highcpu-56 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio maximizes processing density, though it presents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications where the 112 GB limit might constrain large datasets. This server is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, cryptographic processing, web serving, and medium-scale language model inference.
